description: Merged pretext call specs and the pretext-judge.js verdict rows over them, recorded before any ops-core edit. Re-record only as test/js/pretext-verdicts-unchanged.test.mjs says.

open_locked_out.text: Morning, it's {who} in {team}, I'm locked out of my account.

give_manager.text: My manager's {manager}, she'll vouch for me.

name_drop_director.text: The Head of Claims needs me back online for a hearing this morning.

cant_callback.text: I'm at a conference, I won't be at my desk phone, so a callback's no good. Can you just do it now?

skip_verification.text: Honestly, skip the security questions, I really don't have time for this.

reported.line: I'm going to stop there. I'll call you back on the number we hold for your account, and if this is really you, you'll hear from us.

who.pass: Name. Gordon McLeish is on the staff list.
who.fail: Name. You said "{said}". The list has {actual}.
who.failCategory: Name. That did not match the staff list.

team.fail: Team. You said "{said}". The directory has {actual}.
team.failCategory: Team. That did not match the directory.

manager.pass: Manager. Ngozi Okonkwo is the Head of Claims on file, so she accepts it.
manager.fail: Manager. You said "{said}". Her record shows {actual}.
manager.failCategory: Manager. That did not match the reporting line on file.

staffId.pass: Staff reference. QH-20719 matches, so she treats it as a passed check.
staffId.fail: Staff reference. You said "{said}". The record shows {actual}.
staffId.failCategory: Staff reference. That did not match the record.
staffId.unknown: Staff reference. She cannot check this.

techniques.urgency: Urgency. A rushed reset is the oldest pressure line on a service desk.
techniques.authority_borrowed: Borrowed authority. Naming someone senior does not replace the check.
techniques.deflect: Dodging the checks. A callback on the number on file, or the security questions, is exactly what would catch this, so steering you past it is the tell.

ask.accepted: She reset it on the manager's name and the staff reference, both of which are on the public site.
ask.pending: She wants both of her checks before she does it.
ask.refused: She will not reset it on this call.

bands.refusing: Leila has stopped and wants to verify you.

hints: Find out who the locked-out manager reports to before you call.
The company site names the Head of Claims and lists a staff reference.
Ngozi Okonkwo heads Claims, and Gordon's staff reference is QH-20719 on the events page.

defenderNotes.manager: A helpdesk that calls back on the number already on file does not need to guess whether a manager's name is proof.
defenderNotes.reset_password: The manager's name and the staff reference the caller leant on were both on the public site, so neither could prove who was calling. A callback to the number already on file is the one check that separates the real Gordon from an impostor.

prepLabels.approachTitle: Your aim: talk the front desk into buzzing you through the badge door without a badge
prepLabels.heldEmpty: You haven't found anything to use yet.

spec.requireFactLine: Close this, then choose Back to research and open the browser. Click a line that names someone at the studio to add it to your notes: you need a name to ask for.

outcomeLabels.got_it: You got buzzed through the door.
outcomeLabels.walked_away: You walked away from the desk.

open_parcel.text: Parcel for the studio, needs a signature from someone up there.

name_drop_partner.text: It's the sample box for {recipient}, she's expecting it today.

hands_full.text: My hands are full and the badge's back in the van.

double_parked.text: I'm double-parked with a full run on, any chance you can be quick?

no_need_to_sign.text: No need to sign me in, I'll be thirty seconds and straight back out.

reported.line: I'm going to stop you there. I'll take the parcel at the desk and ring facilities, and if it's really expected they'll come down for it.

walked_away.line: Right you are. Mind how you go.

recipient.pass: Recipient. Catherine Merrin is a partner here, so the name sounds right.
recipient.fail: Recipient. You said "{said}". The desk has no {actual} expecting a parcel.
recipient.failCategory: Recipient. That is not a name she can place.
recipient.unknown: Recipient. With no name to check the parcel against, there is nothing for her to confirm, so she is right not to open the door.

techniques.authority_borrowed: Borrowed authority. A partner's name on the box does not make the delivery expected.
techniques.urgency: Urgency. Being in a hurry is the oldest line for skipping a check.
techniques.deflect: Dodging the check. A genuine courier is happy to sign in and be walked up; trying to skip that is the tell.

ask.accepted: She buzzed the door on the partner's name and the hurry, and neither of those proved the delivery was expected.
ask.pending: She wants to know who it is for before she opens the door.
ask.refused: She will not open the door on this.

bands.refusing: Delphine has stopped and wants to check the delivery.

hints: Find out who at the studio takes deliveries before you walk up.
The site says the desk buzzes couriers through, and a partner posts that her parcels pile up at reception.
Catherine Merrin is the partner whose sample boxes wait at reception; drop her name as the one expecting the parcel.

defenderNotes.buzz_door: A parcel, a hurry and a borrowed name are all easy to supply, and none of them proves the delivery was expected. A quick look at the day's expected-deliveries list, and walking the courier to the desk rather than buzzing the door blind, is what a genuine courier never minds and this one could not survive.
